candidates.source_name: CeJN - Elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (portal javne nabavke, tenderi)
candidates.why_relevant: Current official Montenegrin e-procurement system. Contracting authorities (state bodies, municipalities, state-owned enterprises, Posta Crne Gore, EPCG, and the Central Bank itself) publish contract notices and awards here. Tenders for 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'kartice', 'termalne rolne', 'obrada kartichnih transakcija' and cash-handling equipment reveal demand, incumbent suppliers, contract values and renewal cycles that private-bank procurement never discloses.
candidates.access_status: public, likely free search without login; bidding requires registration
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyword/CPV-code search of the notice list; capture notice metadata (authority, CPV, value, deadline, award). Fetch of the root page returned a near-empty SPA shell, so a headless browser or the underlying JSON endpoint is likely needed rather than plain HTTP scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on procurement portal name + ATM/POS terms
queries_used: portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora CRPS bankomat POS terminal tender

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch annual public-procurement reports (PDF) and the 'EU tenderi' category feed; snowball to the list of contracting authorities.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Montenegrin consumer price/fee COMPARISON site (independent of the regulator) for cards, ATM withdrawal or POS/merchant service fees was found - no ME equivalent of a kamatica/kamate-style comparison portal surfaced in local-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the CBCG statutory comparison tables and occasional bankar.me fee journalism cover this need; no independent comparison aggregator identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Merchant-side pricing (MSC/MDR, terminal rental) therefore has no public comparison channel in ME; pricing intelligence must come from bank tariff PDFs one by one, which is a heavier collection design.

negative_findings.description: The seed acronym 'CRPS' does not correspond to the Montenegrin procurement portal. In ME, CRPS historically denotes the Central Register of Business Entities (Centralni registar privrednih subjekata, now under the Tax Administration / Privredni sud), while the procurement system is CeJN (Centralni elektronski javne nabavke) at cejn.gov.me, with ujn.gov.me as the policy directorate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on 'CRPS ... javne nabavke' returned the company register and unrelated Serbian/Bosnian portals rather than ME tenders.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector keyed on 'CRPS' would miss the actual tender source entirely; the glossary must separate CRPS (company register - itself a useful actor-map source) from CeJN (procurement).

negative_findings.description: Local-language queries for ME procurement and job ads repeatedly return Serbian and Bosnian sources (jnportal.ujn.gov.rs, ejn.gov.ba, addiko.rs), because the language is shared.
negative_findings.result_summary: Roughly half of the top results for 'portal javnih nabavki' / 'oglas za posao ... banka' were RS or BA rather than ME.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated sr-language collector needs a hard country filter (.me domain, 'Crna Gora', ME city names) or it will silently ingest Serbian market data as Montenegrin.

negative_findings.description: The official ME procurement portal cejn.gov.me/tenders is a client-side rendered application; a plain HTTP fetch returned only the string 'CeJN' with no notices, search form or documented API.
negative_findings.result_summary: Content not retrievable by simple fetch. This is a hypothesis of JS-rendering, not evidence the site is dead - it must be re-tested with a headless browser and by inspecting XHR endpoints.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell needs a browser-based or API-based collector, not an HTML scraper; budget for that in collection design.

negative_findings.description: No published ME tender or award specifically for ATMs (bankomati), POS terminals or card processing was located within this run's searches - only a generic mention of thermal rolls for cash registers/POS terminals in aggregator descriptions, which was not confirmed on an official notice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Category existence is plausible but unproven; keyword search inside the portal (not via general web search) is required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise that ME ATM/POS demand is largely invisible to open web search and must be reached by in-portal CPV/keyword querying plus indirect channels.

negative_findings.description: No ME-specific national payments/cards industry AWARD programme (e.g. a domestic 'best card product' or 'best ATM network' award) was identified; awards touching ME banks are international titles (Global Finance, Euromoney, The Banker) reported second-hand by local media.
negative_findings.result_summary: Awards channel for ME is thin and foreign-issued.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Awards will contribute little independent signal for this market; deprioritise relative to tenders, job ads and regulator fee tables.

coverage_gaps.description: cejn.gov.me tender search could not be exercised (JS-rendered); its filter fields, CPV support, pagination and any JSON endpoint are unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a headless-browser session against cejn.gov.me/tenders, capture network XHRs, and document the query API; then define the CPV/keyword list for ATM/POS/card categories.

coverage_gaps.description: Career pages were confirmed for only one bank (Prva banka CG). The full set of licensed ME banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and MFIs and their individual career/tender pages has not been enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the CBCG bank register and the Registar platnih institucija, then resolve each entity's career page, 'nabavke/tenderi' page and LinkedIn company page into a monitored actor table.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn job postings and company pages for ME banks/PSPs and for regional vendors selling into ME were not examined in this run (login-walled to search engines).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess LinkedIn (and any compliant jobs API) for ME banking/payments roles; if ToS-restricted, rely on the national register plus bank career pages and note the residual blind spot.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal-level contracting authorities (opstine) and other SOEs (e.g. Montenegro Airlines successor, Zeljeznica, water/waste utilities, Uprava prihoda) were not individually enumerated as buyers of payment-acceptance and cash-handling services.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the list of ME contracting authorities from ujn.gov.me and screen each for payment-related procurement history.

coverage_gaps.description: The State Commission for Control of Public Procurement Procedures (Komisija za kontrolu postupka javnih nabavki) publishes appeal decisions that reveal bidders and prices, but its own official site/URL was not located in this run - only a commercial aggregator claiming OCR access to that database.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and verify the Commission's official decision repository (likely under a .gov.me domain) and prefer it over the commercial mirror.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage used sr and en only. Montenegrin-language variants with the specific graphemes (s-with-caron, c-with-acute) were transliterated in queries, and Albanian-language channels (relevant in Ulcinj/Plav and for some employer ads) were not searched at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key job-ad and tender queries with proper diacritics and add a small Albanian-language term set (punesim, banke, terminal) for northern/coastal municipalities.

brief: Montenegro's indirect and weak-signal layer is unusually workable on the pricing and regulator side and unusually hard on the tender side. The Central Bank publishes statutory, repeatedly-updated fee comparison tables (tarife banaka, basic accounts) plus a payment-institution register and a FinTech Hub with strategy and survey documents - all structured, free and high-credibility. Procurement, by contrast, sits behind a JavaScript-rendered portal (cejn.gov.me) with a legacy archive (portalujn.gov.me), a policy directorate (ujn.gov.me) and several commercial aggregators, one of which (etenderi.me) uniquely indexes State Commission appeal decisions that name bidders and prices; private-bank ATM/POS demand surfaces only via SOE buyers such as Posta Crne Gore and EPCG. The job-ad channel is strong and multi-sourced (ZZZCG statutory register, bankar.me sector feed, zaposli.me/careerjet, individual bank career pages), while events and awards are thin - one recurring domestic fintech conference (Infintech, organised by Logate) plus foreign bank-of-the-year titles reported locally. The two structural risks for any collector are the shared-language contamination from Serbian and Bosnian sources, and the CRPS/CeJN naming confusion in the seed terms.
